source.title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Optimization and Generalization for Overparameterized Two-Layer Neural Networks
source.authors: Sanjeev Arora; S. Du; Wei Hu; Zhiyuan Li; Ruo-Song Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes gradient descent training of an overparameterized two-layer ReLU network and reports benchmark experiments, but uses full-batch GD with a fixed second layer rather than the version's SGD or Adam recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper's statements about Zhang et al. (2017) and Du et al. (2018c) are cited prior work, not this study's results. Rows below cover the paper's own convergence theorem and its MNIST/CIFAR convergence-rate experiments. Generalization-error and complexity-measure results do not report training classification error and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes squared-loss convergence in fully connected two-layer ReLU networks with full-batch GD and fixed output weights. None of the versions names this setting: V1 concerns convolutional networks and training classification error; V2 concerns teacher-student local-minimum frequencies at specific relative widths. The study also does not test depth, initialization comparisons, stability-limit dynamics, or batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors characterize GD optimization trajectories and explain faster convergence for true labels, derive a data-dependent generalization bound independent of network width, and prove learnability of a broad class of smooth functions.
record.recipe_differences: Two-layer fully connected ReLU network; full-batch GD on quadratic loss; second-layer weights fixed; experiments use two classes, m = 10,000, κ = 10⁻², and η = 10⁻³.
record.method_sensitivity: Label condition changes convergence rate: true labels converge faster than random labels, and labels aligned with the smallest-eigenvalue eigenvector converge extremely slowly.

fits_no_version.finding: True labels converge faster than random labels in two-class MNIST and CIFAR experiments; alignment with the smallest-eigenvalue eigenvector produces especially slow convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For wide two-layer ReLU networks trained with full-batch GD and fixed output weights, label alignment with larger kernel eigenvalues predicts faster squared-loss convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: The study's own Theorem 4.1 characterizes the training residual through kernel eigenvalues and label projections, up to an additive tolerance, under small-initialization and sufficient-width assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this two-layer fully connected setting, the kernel spectrum and label projections determine the trajectory of squared-loss optimization.

record.problems: The benchmark experiments cover only two classes of MNIST and CIFAR. Figure 1 reports convergence curves without textual terminal training-error values, and no training classification-error numbers are provided. The model fixes the second layer and uses full-batch GD.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own training-error results identified. Figure 2 reports generalization error and a complexity measure as the random-label portion changes, not training error.

untested.parts: Training classification error of sufficiently large convolutional networks using SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including label corruption and comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
Teacher-student spurious-local-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding one or two student neurons within the specified widths.
Depth degradation and its prevention through identity shortcuts or the specified alternative training recipes.
Comparative effects of activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, or orthogonal versus Gaussian weights on training speed and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics near or above stability thresholds, recovery, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Training-speed and learning-rate comparisons with batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Missing terminal classification-error measurements and slower random-label convergence do not justify a limits_scope verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test convolutional networks, SGD or Adam, CIFAR-100, the full CIFAR-10 or MNIST datasets, or early stopping and regularization comparisons. The benchmark experiments use two classes and report loss-convergence plots, not terminal classification-error values.

rows.subject: two-layer ReLU neural network trained by GD
rows.size_stated: m sufficiently large; m = Ω(n⁶/(λ₀⁴κ²δ³)) in Theorem 3.1
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; first-layer weights trained and second-layer weights fixed
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 3.1 gives a geometric upper bound on quadratic training loss under its stated assumptions.
rows.uncertainty: with probability at least 1 − δ over random initialization
rows.note: This is a theoretical convergence guarantee under the stated width, data, and learning-rate assumptions; it does not report a benchmark classification-error value.
rows.check: Theorem 3.1 is explicitly attributed to Du et al. (2018c), with an extension to general initialization scale, and should not be presented as this study's own main result. The contraction factor is 1 − ηλ₀/2, not 1 − ηλ₀². Its fully connected squared-loss guarantee does not establish V1's convolutional training-classification result.
